crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Rolling Forecasts
children.blurb: A rolling forecast is a financial projection that is continually extended as time passes, so that the planning horizon stays a fixed distance ahead rather than shrinking toward a year end.

children.name: External Signals in Revenue Models
children.blurb: External signals in revenue models covers the practice of feeding data from outside a company's own systems into forecasts of sales, bookings and cash.

children.name: Variance Analysis and Explanation
children.blurb: Variance analysis and explanation is the work of comparing what a business actually did against what it planned, then saying why the two differ.

children.name: Capital Spending Decisions
children.blurb: Capital spending decisions in an AI context cover how a company chooses where to commit money for compute, data, talent and tooling, and how those choices are justified to a board or finance committee.

children.name: Zero-Based Budgeting
children.blurb: Zero-based budgeting is a planning method in which every cost line starts at zero and must be justified for the coming period, rather than being carried forward from last year's figure with an adjustment.

sections.body: Forecasting and planning is the part of finance work that turns a company's past numbers and present expectations into a view of what comes next. Artificial intelligence is used here to build rolling forecasts that update as new data arrives, to fold external signals such as customer demand or supplier delays into revenue models, and to draft the first pass of a variance explanation when actuals land against plan. The work is mostly pattern finding and drafting, not judgment. A model can spot that a cost line drifted, group the transactions behind it, and write a plain summary a person then checks. It can also stress a capital spending case across many scenarios faster than a spreadsheet rebuilt by hand.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The mechanics are largely solved. Rebuilding a forecast on a schedule, blending internal actuals with outside indicators, and producing a readable variance note are all things these systems do reliably enough to be useful. What is not solved is the part that matters most, which is knowing when the past stops being a guide. Models learn from history, so they carry old assumptions into new conditions and can sound confident while doing it. Data quality sets the ceiling, and a forecast is only as good as the ledger feeding it. Accountability stays with people, because a model cannot own a number it produced.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the cycle from looking forward to deciding and then explaining. Rolling Forecasts is the starting point, covering how a forecast is kept current instead of fixed once a year. External Signals in Revenue Models takes that forward view and asks what outside the company should shape the revenue line. Variance Analysis and Explanation is the backward look, where actuals meet plan and someone has to say why they diverged. Capital Spending Decisions moves from recurring numbers to large one-off commitments, where the cost of being wrong is higher. Zero-Based Budgeting closes the set by rebuilding a budget from nothing rather than from last year, which tests every assumption the other pages rely on. A reader would go to the first two for the forward view, the third for the reconciliation, and the last two for the decisions that follow.
